**Approved plan + rulings.** Chris approved the 2026-08-17 `implementation_plan.md` with **R1** (calls/emails become full-width neutral cards; only SMS keeps direction-aligned bubbles), **R2** (optimistic items carry only the status the existing send endpoint actually reports; nothing labeled Delivered without confirmation; no reconciliation system), **R3** (Conversation History filter selection persists across contact switches), **R5** (minimal one-line load-error notice) — and **R4 DECLINED**: the conversation `calls` select stays **byte-untouched** (its over-breadth traces to the 2026-04-20 call Info modal removed 2026-05-01; trimming is deferred unrelated cleanup, documented, not done).

**Filter root cause (the reported bug).** The filter compared display labels to record types: `item._type === convoFilter.toLowerCase()` with state `"All" | "Calls" | "SMS" | "Email"` — `"Calls".toLowerCase()` = `"calls"` never matches `_type "call"`, so **the Calls filter always rendered the empty state**. SMS/Email lowercase to exact matches and were proven working by reproduction tests (no second filter root cause exists). Fix: canonical `ConversationFilter = "all" | "call" | "sms" | "email"` + separate label map (`CONVERSATION_FILTERS`) in the new `conversationTypes.ts`; filtering compares `item.kind === filter`; the conversation-only `any[]` became a discriminated union (`CallConversationItem | SmsConversationItem | EmailConversationItem`, source-qualified React keys `call:<id>`/`sms:<id>`/`email:<id>` per the dashboard-callbacks key-collision lesson). Two adjacent proven defects fixed with it: (1) SMS `_ts` had no fallback, so a null `messages.sent_at` produced `NaN` (poisons the sort comparator, renders no timestamp) — builders now fall back `sent_at → created_at` (calls/emails keep their existing chains); (2) the three-source conversation fetch had no catch, so a failed source (`getContactEmails` throws; supabase returns `{error}` without throwing) left the skeleton forever — now one try/catch → console.error + items `[]` + the R5 notice ("Couldn't load conversation history — try reopening this contact."), with returned supabase errors treated as failures per the house rule, never as an empty result.

**Visual redesign (deliberate, scoped divergence from the 2026-05-01 "dialer ConversationHistory parity" rule — this surface only; the Dialer component and shared `MessageComposePanel` are untouched).** Only SMS keeps iPhone bubbles: outbound right `bg-[#007AFF]` white (the documented intentional literal), inbound left now **token-based `bg-muted border-border`** (replacing the hex `#E9E9EB`/`#262629` grays — same token-regression class this file was fixed for on 2026-05-01; dark-mode-correct by construction). **Calls** = full-width neutral event card (`bg-card border-border`): emerald `PhoneIncoming`/`PhoneOutgoing` chip, "Inbound/Outbound Call", disposition badge (neutral `bg-muted`) or muted status, m:ss duration, timestamp, existing recording toggle → `RecordingPlayer callId compact` (gating rule unchanged: `recording_url` set and not `__recording_pending__`; URLs/storage/auth untouched), Details. **Emails** = compact neutral card: violet `Mail` chip, "Email · Inbound/Outbound", subject (line-clamp-2, "(No subject)" fallback), From/To summary line, timestamp, preserved body expand/collapse (incl. `>`-quoted dimming + capped scroll region), Details. Per-channel empty states ("No activity yet" / "No calls yet" / "No text messages yet" / "No emails yet"). **Wrap hardening:** SMS body carries `[overflow-wrap:anywhere]` + `min-w-0` chain — unlike `break-word`, `anywhere` participates in min-content sizing, so an unbroken string can no longer widen the bubble/card past a narrow column (reproduced in the harness at 390px pre-fix).

**Inline endpoint Details (every item, one interaction).** Shared `DetailsToggleButton` (native button, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, channel-named `aria-label`, focus ring) + inline `DetailsPanel` `<dl>` grid — no modal. SMS: From/To (`formatPhoneNumber`)/Direction/Sent/Status. Calls: Contact number (`contact_phone`)/AgentFlow number (`caller_id_used` — existing semantics, values never rewritten)/Direction/Started/Ended (when present)/Duration/Status/Disposition (when present). Email: From/To/CC+BCC (only when present)/Direction/Sent-or-Received/Delivery status. Missing values render "—"; **no UUIDs, provider IDs, or storage paths are rendered**; zero per-item queries — data comes from the rows already fetched. Query expansion was exactly the plan's minimum: `messages` select + `to_number, status, created_at`; `getContactEmails` select + `cc_emails, bcc_emails`; **calls select byte-untouched (R4)**.

**Optimistic items (net-new area — no prior WORK_LOG precedent).** The optimistic email previously dropped the subject (timeline showed "(No subject)" until reload). Now `handleSendMessage` captures the exact sent values before clearing state and builds the item via `buildOptimisticEmailItem`: real subject, body, outbound, From = the selected connection's `provider_account_email`, To = contact email, now-timestamp, delivery status `"sent"` — truthful because `email-send-contact-message` returns `success:true` only after a provider-confirmed send recorded as `delivery_status:"sent"` (read-only inspection; failure paths never create the item). Optimistic SMS now carries the E.164 From/To actually sent plus **the row id and Twilio status echoed back by `twilio-sms`** (`result.message_id`/`result.status`, default absent → "—"); nothing invented (R2). No reconciliation system — items are still replaced wholesale on the next contact load.

2026-08-11 | [CONTACT-NAME BOUNDARY FIX — branch `claude/agentflow-contact-name-fix-46abvk` from `main` `ef2ff8a`; frontend-only; **no migration, no Edge deploy, no RLS change, no production access or mutation, no backfill of existing rows**] `calls.contact_name = "undefined undefined"` on the non-campaign quick-call path fixed at the contact-model boundary, forward-only

**Scope, as approved by Chris.** F1–F5 + R1 + R2. **R3 (CampaignDetail) and R4 (deep-link save/refetch reorder) were explicitly declined and are NOT in this change.** Chris's stated goal, verbatim: existing stored labels are not to be fixed — *"the goal is only to make sure this does not keep happening on NEW calls going forward."* No historical `calls` / `appointments` row was read, repaired, or backfilled.

**Root cause (verified line-by-line, not inferred).** `ContactDeepLinkPage` fetched with `select("*")` (`:45-50`) and passed the RAW snake_case row straight into `FullScreenContactView` (`:129`), which reads canonical camelCase throughout — so its Call button interpolated `` `${contact.firstName} ${contact.lastName}` `` (`:918`) into the literal **"undefined undefined"**. `FloatingDialer` split that on `" "` (`:261`) and recombined it (`:625`); `TwilioContext.makeCall` snapshotted it into `calls.contact_name` (`:2187`). **The Twilio path was healthy** — steps 4–6 transported faithfully what step 3 handed them. Nothing in the single-leg `device.connect()` architecture was implicated or touched.

**Wider blast radius from the same single cause, also repaired by the mapping:** the record header/avatar rendered blank; `prefillContactName` fed **"undefined undefined"** into `AppointmentModal`, which writes `appointments.contact_name` — a SECOND wrong-name write target; and Save validated `editForm.firstName/lastName/phone` (all `undefined` on a raw row), so **editing a deep-linked contact always failed** with "First name is required". `contact.assignedAgentId` was likewise `undefined`, so the assigned-agent lookup never ran.

**Second confirmed instance (R1).** `CalendarPage.handleOpenContact` did `select('*')` then `data as unknown as Lead` — a cast that was not true — into the same view. Same bug, same Call button, same snapshot.

**Adjacent contract defect (R2).** Both Contacts Kanban `onCall` handlers dispatched a raw `quick-call` event with **no `type`**, and `FloatingDialer` defaults a missing type to `"lead"` — so every recruit quick-call from the Recruits Kanban was written as `calls.contact_type = 'lead'`.

**Files changed (8 source + 5 new tests + 2 docs).** NEW `src/lib/contact-name.ts` (pure `sanitizeContactName` / `contactDisplayName`; no React, no Supabase, no DB lookup) · `src/pages/ContactDeepLinkPage.tsx` (raw row → canonical mapper in both fetch sites; query, `organization_id` scope and `.maybeSingle()` unchanged; **`handleUpdate`'s existing refetch-then-save ordering preserved verbatim per the R4 exclusion**) · `src/lib/supabase-recruits.ts` (**`export`** added to `rowToRecruit` — reuse, not a competing mapper; body byte-unchanged) · `src/components/contacts/FullScreenContactView.tsx` (Call → canonical `dispatchQuickCall` + `contactDisplayName`; `prefillContactName` → same helper) · `src/contexts/TwilioContext.tsx` (**one line**: `contact_name: sanitizeContactName(opts?.contactName) || null`, plus its import) · `src/pages/CalendarPage.tsx` (`rowToLead(data)`) · `src/pages/Contacts.tsx` (both Kanban `onCall` → `dispatchQuickCall` with explicit `"lead"` / `"recruit"`).

**Sanitizer design.** Per-token, **case-sensitive** filtering of exactly `undefined` / `null` — the lowercase tokens a template literal emits. `"undefined undefined"` / `"null null"` / whitespace-only → `""` → persisted as **NULL**, never a literal or an empty string; `"Charlotte undefined"` → `"Charlotte"` (keeps the real half); the genuine surname **"Null"** and `"Undefined Jones"` pass through untouched. `contactDisplayName` reads canonical camelCase first and falls back to snake_case, so a future un-mapped caller still yields a real name. A nameless contact stays dialable (`name: ""`, `contact_name` NULL) — velocity is never blocked for a missing label.

**No user-facing behaviour change — and one was deliberately REMOVED before the PR.** An earlier revision of this change had the Call button surface *"This contact has no dialable phone number."* and skip the `contact_activities` "Call initiated" write when no call could start. Chris ruled that out of scope: this PR fixes the identity snapshot only. The activity write is therefore restored to **unconditional and first**, exactly as before, and the no-phone path is once again a silent no-op with no new toast. The only residual difference on that path is inherent to the canonical helper Chris asked for: `dispatchQuickCall` requires at least one digit, so a phone string with no digits at all no longer opens the dialer on an undialable number (previously the event was dispatched and the listener accepted it). Regression coverage pins the restored behaviour in both directions.

2026-08-09 | [PR #353 RUNBOOK-SAFETY CORRECTION — branch `repair/migration-baseline`, one additive commit on top of `d139790`; **PR kept DRAFT**; **no production contact or mutation, no database command of any kind**] Inverse-B restoration made failure-safe: stage-and-validate before delete, ON_ERROR_STOP everywhere

**Why.** The prior inverse-B block (`BEGIN → DELETE → \copy → COMMIT`, no ON_ERROR_STOP) was unsafe: `\copy` reads a **client-side** file, so a missing/unreadable/malformed snapshot could fail after the DELETE and psql could continue to COMMIT an **emptied** migration-history table.

**Corrected design (documentation only; never executed):** (1) `shasum -a 256 -c` re-verification of the S1-recorded checksum immediately before restoration, abort on mismatch; (2) absolute permission-restricted snapshot path outside the repository (`~/agentflow-operator/…`, S1 now records the checksum in `shasum -c` format); (3) fail-fast both in-script (`\set ON_ERROR_STOP on`) and at invocation (`psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f restore_schema_migrations.sql`); (4) the snapshot is `\copy`-staged into a **session-local temporary table** (`create temporary table … (like supabase_migrations.schema_migrations) on commit drop` — pg_temp only, no application schema change) **before any live row is touched**, so a file/parse failure aborts with the live rows intact; (5) staged rows validated inside the transaction before the delete — count exactly **262**, versions non-null, unique, range `20240401 … 20260805090000`; (6) only then `DELETE` + six-named-column `INSERT … SELECT` from the validated staging table, one transaction — any failure at any step aborts and leaves the original rows intact; (7) the post-restoration identical-ordered-query re-export with **byte-for-byte SHA-256 equality** against the pre-S1 export is preserved, verifying all six columns (`version, statements, name, created_by, idempotency_key, rollback`) including NULLs and array contents, plus the row-count/version-list/migration-list/schema-fingerprint checks.

**Verification (docs pass):** rg confirms ON_ERROR_STOP (in-script + invocation), temporary staging, pre-delete validation, and the six-column restoration are all present · `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0 · literal `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` exit 0 · diff confined to implementation_plan.md, the runbook, and WORK_LOG.md.

**Root cause (proven against live code + live database).** `ImportLeadsPage.handleCampaignCreated` (`:143-155`) created the import campaign with a direct table INSERT writing only `name, type, description, status, total_leads, organization_id, created_by`. The prop contract was the structural defect: `onCampaignCreated: ({name, type, description})` (`ImportLeadsModal.tsx:207`) **had no agent field at all**. `campaigns.user_id` therefore fell to `DEFAULT auth.uid()` — and had to, because live RLS `campaigns_insert` is `WITH CHECK (organization_id = get_org_id() AND user_id = auth.uid())`, so a browser insert **cannot** create an agent-owned campaign. `add_leads_to_campaign`'s Personal branch (`lead.assigned_agent_id IS DISTINCT FROM campaigns.user_id`) then skipped all 106 leads (owned by `812e26e7…`, campaign owned by the Admin `ecf2bb91…`), returning `{added:0, skipped:106}` with HTTP 200 and no error. `finalize_contact_import` computed `tagged(0)=added(0)` AND `added+skipped(106)=attempted(106)` → **`completed_with_skips`**, and `ImportLeadsModal.tsx:1656-1659` gated the green `CheckCircle2` and the words "Import Complete!" **solely on `savingProvenance`**, never on the status. Production evidence: `import_history d7811230-abf6-47b5-bf8b-6aacfac976ef`, campaign `8b680353-d9c8-4d1c-a479-d29896bde760` (Personal, `user_id=ecf2bb91…`, `assigned_agent_ids=[]`, 0 queue rows), all 106 leads alive and assigned to `812e26e7…`.

**Corrective pass #2 — PR #352 review items 1-8 (2026-08-07, same branch, second commit).** (1) **Saved/resumed dialer sessions are now authorized.** `start_dialer_session` authorized only the SUPPLIED campaign and then returned any existing active session without checking that session's own `campaign_id` — so `start_dialer_session(NULL)` skipped the guard entirely and resumed an unauthorized Personal session, and an authorized request could still be satisfied by a stale unauthorized one. The reuse branch now re-authorizes `v_session.campaign_id` (raises 42501) and refuses a non-null requested campaign that differs from the active session's. **No session is ended, abandoned or rewritten** — `T34c` asserts it is still `active` after both refusals, so telemetry (`dialer_sessions`, invariant #12) is untouched. `useDialerSession` gained `activeSessionCampaignRef` so `startServerSession` short-circuits ONLY for the same campaign — cached state can no longer bypass server revalidation. `CampaignDetail` stores the dial answer WITH the campaign id it was resolved for and derives it during render, closing the one-render window where the previous route's `true` authorized a newly navigated campaign. It now enforces the approved matrix (Personal: owner/Admin/SA/canonical TL · Team: owner/**listed participant**/Admin/SA/canonical TL · Open Pool: org-wide · cross-org always rejected), with role read from `public.profiles`. (3) **Strategy contract enforced server-side**: `myself` cannot name another owner or other participants; `specific_agent` requires exactly one; `round_robin` requires a non-empty unique set and is rejected for Personal; `unassigned` takes exactly the caller for Team and is rejected for Personal; Open Pool takes no participant list. Plus an **import-only routing precheck** that reads ownership from the database over the immutable imported id set and refuses BEFORE inserting anything (Personal cannot take unassigned or multi-owner sets; Team must cover every assigned lead's agent) — generic non-import callers keep their per-lead skip behaviour and reason-specific response. (4) **Counts are a real partition.** `imported = attached + already_present + ineligible + remaining`, computed from actual rows and `import_history_id` provenance, with the server raising if it does not hold; `attached` now means "created by THIS import", so `already_present` is no longer structurally zero and no longer overlaps. `remaining` is the retryable remainder only — ineligible leads are reported separately and never labelled "still to attach". An import with **no campaign** returns all four as NULL with `has_campaign:false`, so the result screen no longer claims "All imported leads were added to the campaign" / "0 attached" for an import that never targeted one; retry is withheld there too. `applyAttachCounts` no longer hardcodes `alreadyPresent: 0`. (5) **The finalization Zod contract is actually consumed** — schemas moved to `src/lib/import-campaign-schemas.ts` (so `src/lib` no longer depends on a component directory) and `finalizeImport` now parses the envelope and throws instead of `data as unknown as ImportFinalizeResult`. 2026-08-06 | [EMERGENCY TELEPHONY HOTFIX — **INCIDENT CLOSED: DEPLOYED + SIX NUMBERS REPAIRED + LIVE CALL VERIFIED**; committed as `a977fff`, pushed to `hotfix/new-number-outbound-account-owner`, and opened as **draft PR #351** → `main`; `twilio-buy-number` v40 ACTIVE; `repair-twilio-number-ownership` v2 ACTIVE; **NOT merged**; no migration/RLS/RPC/grant/frontend/Vercel change] NEWLY PURCHASED CALLER IDs — immediate hang-up caused by Twilio parent/subaccount ownership mismatch

**Production symptom and isolated proof (read-only).** Six Agency caller IDs purchased at 22:17–22:19 UTC were active in AgentFlow but outbound attempts through two of them ended as false `busy` in 1–3 seconds with duration 0. Against the same destination, an older caller ID completed a 10-second call at 22:31:26, a new ID failed in 1 second at 22:31:50, and another new ID failed in 3 seconds at 22:32:38. Five attempts on one new ID and two on another showed the same pattern while older IDs continued normal completed/no-answer behavior. Numbers remain masked in this log.

**Root cause.** Deployed `twilio-token` v33 correctly signs the browser Voice JWT with the **master** Account SID because the TwiML App is master-owned (the May 5 ConnectionError 53000 hotfix and invariant #1). Deployed `twilio-buy-number` v39 instead used `loadSubaccountCreds()` and purchased each new number inside Chris's organization **subaccount**. The master-account Voice leg then supplied a subaccount-owned `<Dial callerId>`, violating Twilio's caller-ID ownership/verification contract and producing the immediate termination pattern (Twilio 13214 class). The dialer state machine, caller-ID eligibility, queue, call insert, and status telemetry were not the cause and are untouched.

**Emergency design.** Preserve the proven master Voice path. Future purchases use `loadOutboundTwilioCreds()` while the inserted `phone_numbers.organization_id` remains the AgentFlow tenant boundary. A new internal repair function accepts only an explicit bounded UUID list plus organization UUID, requires an exact service-role bearer token, validates every row as active/same-org/PN SID/inside the narrow incident window before any Twilio call, proves the PN is on the expected losing subaccount, transfers it to master, reapplies all Voice/SMS/status callbacks, then GET-verifies master ownership and every callback field. Only after verification does it set that row's `trust_hub_status = 'pending'`. Already-master numbers are idempotently reconfigured/verified; first failure stops and returns earlier successes. Responses/logs omit phone numbers, account credentials, and raw Twilio bodies.

**Trust Hub truthfulness.** The purchase path no longer calls the existing subaccount-scoped Trust Hub assignment for a master-owned number or fabricates `approved`. New and transferred numbers remain `pending`; a proper owning-master registration/assignment path is a separate follow-up. Per-subaccount TwiML Apps/JWTs/signature validation are also deliberately deferred from this incident.

**Tests and verification.** Fail-first was captured before `ownership.ts` existed. Final focused Deno tests **14/14**: exact request bounds/UUIDs, duplicate rejection, exact service-role and workflow-secret authorization (empty/inexact rejected), org/status/SID/incident-window target checks, canonical callback generation, complete ownership/config verification, sanitized bounded Twilio failures, fresh transfer order, idempotent already-master rerun, transfer/configuration/verification aborts, and the invariant that DB status is never updated before full Twilio verification. Deno check clean on `twilio-buy-number`, repair entrypoint, and both test modules (using an uncommitted `/tmp` import map to the installed `@supabase/supabase-js` because direct Deno registry access was blocked) · `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0 · full Vitest **991/991 in 76 files** (initial run without Vite Supabase vars had 9 environment-only collection failures; rerun with non-secret test values green) · targeted ESLint `--max-warnings 0` clean · Vite production build succeeds with only standing chunk-size/dynamic-import warnings · `git diff --check` clean.

Explicitly untouched: `TwilioContext.tsx`, `DialerPage.tsx`, `FloatingDialer.tsx`, caller-ID selection, queue/RPC/locks, `calls.duration`, `twilio-voice-status`, RLS, migrations, dependencies, all frontend files.

Revalidated exactly six targets. Deployed corrected purchase **v40** and repair **v1**, then re-fetched and compared every dependency byte-for-byte to local. The first internal call used `private.twilio_provisioning_config.service_role_key` and was rejected 401; a side-effect-free probe proved `private.workflow_engine_config.service_role_key` is also stale. **Neither request reached body validation or Twilio; zero mutation.** Repair was extended to accept AgentFlow's existing exact `X-Workflow-Secret` / `WORKFLOW_INTERNAL_SECRET` internal path (service-role exact match retained), tested 14/14, and deployed as **v2**. No other row fields were changed.

2026-08-06 | [BUGFIX — LOCALLY IMPLEMENTED on branch `bugfix/leaderboard-metric-switch-rerank` (cut from `origin/main` = `a411892`, the merged PR #347); NOT committed, NOT pushed, NOT merged, NOT deployed; no Supabase, migration, RPC, RLS, grant, Edge Function, Dashboard-widget, TVMode, dialer, or dependency change] LEADERBOARD — metric switches re-rank the cached standings synchronously (zero RPC, one coherent transition)

**Regression (confirmed root cause, post-PR #347).** `get_org_leaderboard_stats` returns every metric in one response, but `metric` sat in the fetch-callback dependency chains (`fetchOrgData`/`fetchGroupData` → `fetchData` → the fetch effect). Switching the metric therefore updated the visible metric immediately, left agents ranked by the previous metric, fired a pointless RPC with a visible `filterRefreshing` state, re-ranked only after the response, and let the podium's per-slot `AnimatePresence mode="sync"` overlap outgoing/incoming cards (0.38s exit ghost) across the two inconsistent renders. Production pg_stat_statements confirmed the RPC itself is healthy (64 calls, 42.15 ms mean) — frontend lifecycle/rendering only. Audit also verified three co-defects: the podium `OdometerValue` rolled between semantically unrelated values on switch (old number through the new formatter, then a 0.48s tween); table rows spring-glide on ANY reorder (`layout="position"` is unconditional); and the filter-reset effect never cleared `rankAnimations`/`rankMotions`/`rankDeltas`/`newLeaderId` (only their 1.4–2.8s timers did), so a live update ≤1.5s before a switch left stale glow/pop/glide on the recomposed board.

**Fix (surgical, 2 production files).** `useLeaderboardData.ts`: new synchronously-current **`metricRef`** + controlled **`changeMetric`** exposed under the existing `setMetric` API — no-ops on same-metric; **clones** the cached rows (`agentsRef.current.map(a => ({...a}))` — existing state objects never mutated) and `rankAgents` them by the new metric; clears ALL live-animation state (`rankAnimations`/`rankMovements`/`rankMotions`/`rankDeltas`/`newLeaderId`/`spotlightAgentId`) synchronously; commits metric + ranked rows in ONE React 18 batch so no render can pair the new metric with the old ordering. **Zero fetches, no `beginFetch`, no spinner.** `metric` removed from both fetch dependency arrays; fetch completions rank and animate with `metricRef.current`, so a poll resolving after a switch ranks by the LATEST metric (never a stale closure) and a superseded stale response stays discarded by the existing generation guard. Period and view/group changes still fetch (their data scope changes); 4s polling, realtime refresh, `fetchGenerationRef`, `loadError`/retry, and Recent Wins untouched. `Leaderboard.tsx`: **`key={metric}`** on `LeaderboardPodium` and `LeaderboardRankingsTable` — because the re-rank commits with the metric, the key remounts both subtrees in that same commit: no `AnimatePresence` exit-ghost overlap (disabled ONLY for filter-driven changes), no enter animation (`initial={false}`), no table layout glide, and `OdometerValue` re-seeds (no cross-metric roll). Live commits never change the key, so every live-data glide/glow/spotlight/odometer behavior is preserved exactly. Deliberately untouched (audit-backed): Dashboard `LeaderboardWidget` (no metric switcher, doesn't use the hook) and `TVMode` (its 30s rotation is local state + a local synchronous re-sort already); podium/card/odometer/rank-motion/table components; `leaderboardTypes` (`rankAgents` stays deterministic: metric ↓, last/first name, id).

**Tests — fail-first proven.** 7 new hook tests (fixture: A leads Policies, B leads Calls, C leads Talk Time): against unmodified source **6/7 failed** exactly on the defect (stale ordering after switch, extra RPC, `filterRefreshing` true, stale-closure poll ranking, uncleaned animation maps) with the period-still-fetches guard passing pre- and post-fix. After the fix: **18/18 hook**, 31/31 focused (hook+page+widget). Coverage: immediate B-rank-1 on Policies→Calls; identity/value association through the switch; zero RPC; no loading state; rapid-switch settling (final Calls ordering, zero RPC); post-switch poll ranked by latest metric; superseded stale response cannot restore the old ordering; period-change fetch lifecycle intact; synchronous animation-state clearing.

**Verification (all green, exact figures).** `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0 · focused suites **31/31 in 3 files** · full `npx vitest run` host TZ **944/944 in 70 files** (937 baseline + 7 new, zero regressions) · `TZ=UTC` **932 passed | 12 skipped (944)** (known `laOnly` DST skips) · `TZ=America/Los_Angeles` **944/944** · ESLint `--max-warnings 0` clean on all 3 touched files · `npm run build` succeeds · `git diff --check` clean. NOT verified: authenticated browser run (standing environment limitation — placeholder credentials land on `/login`); the visual transition should be eyeballed on the PR preview at review time.

**Files.** EDITED: `src/hooks/useLeaderboardData.ts` (+39/−7), `src/pages/Leaderboard.tsx` (+7), `src/hooks/__tests__/useLeaderboardData.test.tsx` (+202), `implementation_plan.md`, `WORK_LOG.md`. No new file. **Migrations: none · Supabase changes: none · RLS changes: none · Deployments: none · Commits/pushes: none.**

**Remaining risks.** The `key={metric}` remount intentionally drops any in-flight live animation at the switch instant (mandated) and resets transient hover state inside the two remounted components — no scroll container lives inside them. Leftover-animation clearing is implemented for the metric path only; period/view switches keep today's timer-based decay (pre-existing, out of scope). **Next steps:** Chris's separate approval to commit + push + open a PR; merge/deploy separately (frontend-only — no migration involved).

**Root cause (two defects).** (1) `useOnboardingPageFlow.ts` cast any array to `string[]` (`Array.isArray(ls) ? (ls as string[]) : []`), but the invitation flow (InviteUserModal → `usersSupabaseApi.invite` → `invite-user` → `invitations.licensed_states` → `accept-invite` → auth metadata → `profiles.licensed_states`) stores `{state, licenseNumber}` objects; `LicensedStatesMultiSelect` then rendered each entry as a React child inside a chip `<li>` → error #31. (2) Latent data loss: completion wrote the UI string selection back unconditionally, which would have replaced `[{state:"CA",licenseNumber:"12345"}]` with `["California"]`, destroying the license number. Data-contract bug — the data is valid, the onboarding reader was wrong (migration `20260522212000_backfill_legacy_licenses.sql` proves strings, objects, abbreviations and DC all already existed in prod in 2026-05).

**Fix — adapter boundary, not UI suppression.** New pure functions in `src/components/onboarding/licensedStates.ts`, all parsing from `unknown` (types `LicensedStateObjectEntry` / `LicensedStateProfileEntry`; no new `any`):
- `normalizeLicensedStateName` — trimmed, case-insensitive full-name or 2-letter-code → canonical full name, else null (mapping = new `US_STATE_CODES` / `US_STATE_NAME_BY_CODE` / `US_STATE_CODE_BY_NAME` in `src/constants/us-geo.ts`, zipped positionally from the existing `US_STATE_NAMES`; no settings-feature import, no package).
- `licensedStatesToUiSelection` — unknown → safe deduped ordered `string[]` of full names (strings and `{state}` objects recognized; null/numbers/empty/objects-without-state dropped; unrecognized states excluded from UI but not destroyed).
- `isLicensedStatesSelectionUnchanged` — SET equality vs the normalized baseline, so remove-then-re-add still counts unchanged.
- `rebuildLicensedStatesPayload` — modified selections only: still-selected object entries re-emitted verbatim (clone; license number + extra keys intact; the license-number-bearing duplicate wins), retained legacy strings become canonical full names (D3), new states use `{state: CODE, licenseNumber: ""}` when the source had any object entry else full-name strings, deselected states dropped, unrecognized-but-real entries (DC, typos) appended verbatim (D2 — the user never saw them so they cannot have deselected them).

**Hook (`useOnboardingPageFlow.ts`).** Raw payload retained in `originalLicensedStatesRef`; load path uses `licensedStatesToUiSelection` (unsafe cast deleted); completion adds `licensed_states` to the patch ONLY when the selection set changed (D1 — an untouched selection omits the key entirely, so `updateProfile`'s plain `.update()` never rewrites the stored value). Timezone branching, founder/invite branching, org/company-settings writes, auth-metadata update, `savingRef` duplicate-submit guard, and the `/dashboard` redirect are untouched.

**LicensedStatesMultiSelect.tsx deliberately NOT edited** — the `string[]` contract is enforced at the data boundary; an in-component filter would be the forbidden UI-only suppression and would mask future contract violations.

**Adversarial review pass (14-agent multi-lens review + per-finding refutation, run before commit) — three real defects found in the first cut of the adapter, all fixed and pinned by tests:**
1. **Duplicate same-state entries lost the losing license.** The keep-one rule collapsed `[{CA,"111"},{CA,"222"}]` to one entry, deleting `"222"`; worse, a non-string license (`{CA, licenseNumber: 12345}`) was coerced to `""` so an EMPTY duplicate could win over it. Rebuild now re-emits **every distinct real license value** per still-selected state (`licenseKeyOf` treats any non-null non-string as license-bearing), collapsing only exact-same-license duplicates.
2. **License-bearing entries without a usable `state` were deleted on any rebuild** (`{licenseNumber:"K-77"}`, `{state:"",licenseNumber:"Q-11"}`, `{state:9,...}`, tuple `["CA","L-9"]`). Parse classification widened: only provably valueless entries (null, numbers, booleans, empty strings, `{}`, `[]`) are dropped; any object/array still carrying data is opaque and re-emitted verbatim.
3. **Torn baseline in `finish()`.** The baseline ref was read AFTER `await refreshSessionUntilClaimsReady()`, whose TOKEN_REFRESHED events make AuthContext refetch the profile and re-run the load effect mid-completion — a concurrent admin grant could be rebuilt away. `finish()` now snapshots the baseline synchronously before any await, pairing it with the click-time selection closure.
Review also mutation-tested the suites and found the empty-selection rebuild path and the malformed-licenseNumber contract unpinned (a mutant dropping opaque entries on Clear survived all 889 tests), plus one invite-suite override that silently dropped the object fixture — all three closed with explicit tests (popover **Clear** over an opaque-entry profile now asserts the DC license survives in the patch).

**Tests — fail-first proven.** The integration suite was written and run against the unmodified baseline BEFORE the fix: 12/13 failed, the crash tests with the exact production error `Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {state, licenseNumber})`. **Why.** A third review of PR #343 found two React-correctness defects I introduced and one test I had weakened without restoring. All three are fixed. Earlier entries are unchanged.

**1. Duplicate React keys on callback rows.** The callback mapping set `id: row.contactId ?? row.key` and the list rendered `key={item.id || idx}`, so render identity was the **contact id** and `NormalizedCallbackRow.key` — built specifically to be unique across merged sources — was discarded. Two callbacks for one contact therefore collided, which is an ordinary case: a campaign callback plus a quick-call callback for the same lead is exactly what the dual-source union exists to surface. Reproduced against the pre-fix head as `Warning: Encountered two children with the same key, '1ead0000-…-00000000000a'` — the warning naming the **contact UUID** was the proof.

**Fix:** the mapping now carries **`__rowKey: row.key`** (source-qualified `campaign:<id>` / `appointment:<id>`) and the fragment renders `key={item.__rowKey ?? item.id ?? idx}`. `id` and `contact_id` are untouched, so contact identity, navigation and dialing are unchanged, and non-callback rows keep their previous `item.id ?? idx` behavior. Overwriting `id` with `row.key` was deliberately rejected — `id` is read as a contact identity via the `__idIsContact` path, so that would have reintroduced a non-contact value into contact identity.

**2. No stale-request protection.** `DashboardDetailModal` had **zero** cancellation or generation guards (the widget had them; the modal, which actually has pagination plus a type/range/scope switch plus an open/close lifecycle, did not). An older initial or paginated request could resolve after a newer one began, or after the modal closed, and still call `setData`, `setLoadError`, `setPageError`, `setHasMore`, `setLoading` or `setIsFetchingNextPage`.

**Fix:** `requestGenerationRef` increments on every new initial request and in effect cleanup. Each request captures its generation and checks `isStale()` before **every** state write — success, early-return, catch and finally. A stale `finally` no longer clears loading state belonging to a newer request. Pagination inherits the current generation without incrementing it, so a page result belongs to the initial load it was requested under.

**3. Pagination was not actually serialized.** React state is not a synchronous lock: two scroll events in the same tick both observe `isFetchingNextPage === false` before any rerender and both fire the same next page.

**Fix:** `paginationLockRef` holds `{ generation, page }`. At most one pagination request per generation; only the acquiring request in the owning generation may release it; a new initial generation or cleanup clears it. `isFetchingNextPage` remains the rendered UI state but is no longer the guard, and `handleScroll` gates on the ref.

**4. Requirement 26 was not tested.** The test named for it asserted only that the initial page rendered — no injected second-page error, no scroll trigger, no assertions on the failure notice or the surviving rows. I weakened it while fixing an unrelated `getByText` multi-match failure and never restored it. It is **removed and replaced** by a real component flow: full 20-row first page with distinct lead ids → error injected only after initial completion → explicit `scrollTop`/`scrollHeight`/`clientHeight` geometry → shipped scroll event → wait for "Couldn't load more records" → all 20 rows still visible → "Couldn't load these records", "No intelligence found in this range" and "End of list" all absent → no `permission denied` / `42501` / `check RLS` / table name anywhere in the DOM.

**Both new regression tests were verified to FAIL against the unfixed code.** Reverting only the render key fails the duplicate-key test; reverting only the lock fails the serialization test. The three scroll events are batched inside a single `act()` — sequential `fireEvent` calls each flush state, which masked the race in a first attempt and would have shipped a test that proved nothing.

For a personally-filtered agent the union was canonical-only in practice.

**Final predicate** — `(user_id = uid) OR (user_id IS NULL AND created_by = uid)`. `user_id` is authoritative whenever populated; `created_by` is a compatibility fallback **only** when `user_id IS NULL`, and never rescues a row whose `user_id` belongs to another user. Two chained `.eq()` calls AND, so PostgREST's logical tree is required: `.or("user_id.eq.<uid>,and(user_id.is.null,created_by.eq.<uid>)")`, emitted from the single exported `ownershipOrExpression()`. Campaign branches keep `callback_agent_id` only; Admin/Team stays unfiltered with zero ownership predicate; no hierarchy expansion.

**`.or()` interpolates a RAW, non-parameterized filter string** (unlike `.eq()`), so `assertValidUserId()` UUID-validates the id first and **throws before any query executes** — never by silently dropping the ownership filter, which would widen the result to the whole organization. This is the repo's first PostgREST `.or()` (a grep found `.or(` only in Zod schemas), so a test asserts the exact emitted string, not just the row outcome.

**Production currently has zero Scheduled Follow Up / Call Back rows and zero null-`user_id` rows.** That is explicitly **not** treated as evidence the writer is safe — only that no quick-call callback has been scheduled yet. Correctness is proven by the fixture truth table.

[])` / `(res?.count ?? 0)`, and `dashboard-contact-identity.ts` did the same with `result.data ?? []`. Three wrong outcomes followed: a failed row query rendered "No pending callbacks" / "No intelligence found in this range"; a failed count silently reported 0; and — worst — a failed contact lookup was **mis-attributed as a deleted contact**, because an empty map is exactly the signal `normalizeCampaignRow` reads as dangling.

**Error contract.** One shared `DashboardQueryError` + `assertNoQueryError()`, exported from `dashboard-contact-identity.ts` (chosen deliberately: `dashboard-callbacks.ts` already imports from it, so no new module and no circular dependency). `{ data: [], error: null }` is a **successful empty** result meaning "none found"; `error !== null` **rejects the whole operation**. Checked on all 3 row branches, all 3 exact-count branches, and all 6 contact-table lookups (both resolvers). No partial page, no partial sum, and a failed lookup never becomes a dangling identity. The user-facing message is generic; the raw Supabase error is retained as `cause` for `console.error` only and is never rendered.

**Stale-JWT behavior preserved.** A policy that matches no rows returns `{ data: [], error: null }`, not an error, so the documented `campaign_leads` stale-role-claim case still reports **"none found"** (invariant #19/#22). Pinned by a test that returns empty campaign branches alongside a populated appointment branch and asserts it resolves.

**3. The failure block renders **before** the empty state, making "No pending callbacks" unreachable after an error. `DashboardDetailModal` gained `loadError` (initial) and `pageError` (pagination): an initial failure renders "Couldn't load these records", never "No intelligence found in this range"; a pagination failure keeps the rows already loaded but says more failed to load rather than presenting the list as complete. Blocked-reason wording is now neutral — "No linked contact record is available" — because a successful-but-empty lookup can mean RLS visibility rather than deletion.

**4. Component-level failure tests.** The UI requirements are asserted by rendering the shipped components with an injected branch error and proving the failure message appears while the valid-empty message does **not**, and that no raw database detail (message, code, hint, table name) reaches the DOM — not by testing the error class alone.

**1. Canonical quick-call integration.** All three Dashboard widgets were dispatching `"agentflow:open-dialer"` — an event with **zero listeners anywhere in the repo**, so every Dashboard call button was a silent no-op. The payload was also wrong twice over: `contactName` is never read by the listener (the name was lost) and `type` was omitted entirely, so `FloatingDialer.tsx:267` would have labelled every contact `'lead'`. New `src/lib/quick-call.ts` is the one typed dispatcher, emitting exactly `{ contactId, name, phone, type }` on `quick-call` — the contract read from the only listener, matching the working precedent at `Contacts.tsx:2452`. It returns `false` when there is no dialable number so callers cannot report a call that never started. **`TwilioContext.tsx` was not edited**; no REST outbound / two-legged / SIP / Telnyx / `dialer-start-call` path was introduced; `calls.duration` and all Twilio telemetry untouched.

**2. Real contact type resolved, not assumed.** `appointments` has no `contact_type` column and `calls.contact_type` is NULL on 68 of 85 live rows (AGENT_RULES §5), so Callbacks and Missed Calls now resolve phone **and** kind from `leads` + `clients` (clients win a collision — a converted lead's live contact is the client). This is also what lets a client callback dial at all: the previous lead-only lookup left every client contact with an empty phone. `AnniversariesWidget` now selects `phone` (it previously selected none, so its only action could never have worked) and dispatches `type: "client"`.

**3. Nested-action event handling.** Every call/action control now calls `e.stopPropagation()`. On the Dashboard page the root cause was structural: `Dashboard.tsx` put `onClick={handleWidgetClick}` on the `<div>` wrapping `renderWidget(key)`, so every button inside every widget bubbled up and opened the detail modal. The click handler moved to the **card header only**, and `cursor-pointer` is now applied only to headers that actually open a modal.

**4. Correct contact navigation.** `DashboardDetailModal` navigated `calls_today` / `missed_calls` rows with `item.id` — the **`calls` row id** — to a hardcoded `tab=Leads`, so the deep link could never resolve. Added `resolveContactId()` / `resolveContactType()` / `contactsTabFor()`: navigation now uses `contact_id` (already selected by those queries) plus the resolved type, and **fails truthfully with a toast** when a row has no contact link instead of closing the modal and pushing a dead URL.

**5. Invalid `makeCall` removed.** `makeCall(item.phone, undefined, item.id)` passed a **string** into the third parameter, which is `MakeCallOptions` (an object), was never awaited, and toasted success unconditionally even though `undefined` is the documented failure return. (`tsc` missed it because `item` is `any`.) That call site now routes through `dispatchQuickCall` and reports only what actually happened; `useTwilio` is no longer imported by the modal.

**6. Callback query correctness.** Today = **overdue plus due-today** (the deliberate exception in the date rule). Deterministic ordering `start_time ASC, id ASC` so the most overdue is first and ties never swap between renders. Added a bounded 30-day lower bound (the query was historically unbounded) and a **half-open** upper bound. The displayed total now comes from an **exact `count`** over the same predicate — it was previously `data.length`, which capped "View All N Callbacks" at the page size of 15.

**7. Half-open `[start, end)` bounds.** `useDashboardStats` and `DashboardDetailModal` now derive an exclusive end for every period, and the **current** period has an upper bound at all — it previously had none, so the Appointments card counted every future appointment ever booked. Removed the inclusive `.lte` + `setMilliseconds(-1)` / `23:59:59` fudging, and stopped `now`/`today` being mutated in place by `setDate()`. **Agency-timezone derivation is Build 2 and is NOT claimed** — these boundaries are still browser-local; no new browser-local logic was entrenched beyond correcting the bounds themselves.

**8. Widget-preference correctness.** New `src/lib/dashboard-widget-prefs.ts` (pure, unit-tested). `saveLayout` and `resetLayout` previously discarded the Supabase result and toasted success unconditionally — supabase-js **resolves** with `{ error }` rather than throwing, so the `catch` never fired for a database error. Both now inspect the returned error, keep edit mode open on failure, and refuse to write when the pre-read failed (the settings blob is read-modify-write, so writing blind would drop other preferences). A returned load error is now distinguished from "no preferences saved". Normalization drops unknown / removed / duplicated / non-string keys, resolves legacy aliases (incl. `schedule` → `appointments`), **appends** any widget a saved order predates so a new widget still appears, and derives the restore list from `order` so a widget hidden under a stale key can no longer become permanently unrestorable. Reorder, hide, restore and reset all retained; preferences stay personal to the logged-in user.

**9. Default period → Today** (`Dashboard.tsx`, was `month`). **Widget renamed to "Schedule"** (approved D6); the persisted key stays `appointments` and the normalizer accepts a legacy `schedule` alias, so no saved layout is invalidated. `StatCards.tsx` deliberately untouched — outside the authorized file boundary, and renaming a KPI card would touch sales-KPI surface.

**10. Misleading realtime wording removed.** "Real-time Intelligence Feed" and its pulsing dot are gone — **no `supabase.channel(...)` subscription exists anywhere on the Dashboard**; the list is fetched once per open and paginated on scroll. Replaced with an accurate per-type subtitle.

2026-07-31 | [PR OPEN — draft PR #340 on branch `claude/p0-email-release-blockers`, pushed; migration NOT applied; no Edge Function deployed; no production data touched] P0 SECURITY — Profile authorization hardening + signup trust model (email-release blocker)

**What & why.** The adversarial review of the system-email PR ([#338](https://github.com/cgarness/agentflow-life-insure/pull/338)) found that its new authorization gates rest on `profiles.role` / `profiles.is_super_admin` — columns any authenticated user could rewrite on their own row. Investigation confirmed that and found the surface is materially worse than the two reported holes. Chris granted `#APPROVE_RLS_CHANGE` for code + migration only. **PR #338 is blocked until this merges.** Branch cut fresh from `origin/main`; PR #338's branch verified byte-identical to its remote and untouched.

**The actual vulnerability (all verified live, read-only).**
- `profiles_update_own` = UPDATE, **`TO PUBLIC`**, `USING (id = auth.uid())`, **no `WITH CHECK`** — Postgres reuses USING as the check, so any user could set **any** column on their own row.
- **Six permissive policies OR together; zero restrictive.** Patching one would have fixed nothing.
- **Two escalation chains turn a self-edit into real authority:** `on_profile_update` → `set_claim()` → `auth.users.raw_app_meta_data`, where `get_user_role()` gates **109** policies and `get_org_id()` gates **179**; and `custom_access_token_hook` re-mints the same values as JWT claims on refresh. So `UPDATE profiles SET role='Admin', organization_id='<victim org>' WHERE id=auth.uid()` was **cross-tenant account takeover**.
- `profiles_insert` = `TO PUBLIC WITH CHECK (true)` with `anon` holding INSERT and an attacker-chosen `id` (Supabase advisor lint `0024`).
- `twilio_client_identity` is a capability minted into Twilio access tokens with **no unique constraint** — overwriting a peer's value enables inbound-call interception.
- `hierarchy_path` was directly forgeable (its recompute trigger is scoped `UPDATE OF upline_id`); it feeds `is_ancestor_of()`, gating 7 policies across 6 tables.
- `create-user`'s `invite_token` was **write-only** — never read back, so nothing validated existence, status, expiry, or email match; expiry was enforced **nowhere** server-side; a legacy base64 `?invite=` blob supplied org/role unsigned.

**Fix — three independent layers (requirement: not a trigger alone).** (1) **Grants:** `anon` loses everything; `authenticated` keeps SELECT + a **column-scoped** UPDATE excluding `id`, `organization_id`, `hierarchy_path`, `created_at`, `last_login_at`, `twilio_client_identity`, `welcome_email_sent_at`. (2) **RLS:** `profiles_insert` dropped outright (no client INSERT exists anywhere); `profiles_update_own` / `_admin` recreated `TO authenticated` with explicit `WITH CHECK`. (3) **`enforce_profile_field_authorization()`** — a `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE` guard raising only when a protected column *actually changes* and the actor is unauthorized, which is what lets the existing admin UI keep working unchanged. **Trusted source: the actor's own `profiles` row, never the JWT** — the claims are derived from the very columns being protected, so trusting them would let a poisoned claim authorize its own poisoning. Named `trg_00_*` so it fires before the hierarchy recompute. Plus a canonical `profiles_role_check`, and invitations hardening (`invitations_update_status` with `USING (true)` dropped; column-scoped `UPDATE(status)` under a Pending→Revoked policy).

**Signup trust.** Invite mode derives org/role/upline/commission/licensed-states exclusively from the invitation row (Pending + unexpired + exact `lower(trim())` email equality, **never `ilike`**), claimed atomically before the account exists and released if creation fails. Self-serve ignores body authority entirely, mints the org server-side and forces `Admin` **in that new org only**.  The unsigned base64 path is gone. The browser's `signup()` no longer accepts or sends any authority field.

**Adversarial review found 6 defects in the first implementation — all fixed.** Most important: the guard as first written **broke every admin upline change** (the `cascade_hierarchy_update` AFTER trigger's nested descendant writes carry a non-null `auth.uid()`, since SECURITY DEFINER does not reset it) — fixed by comparing against `compute_hierarchy_path(NEW.id)`. And the orphan-org compensation **could never have worked** (41 tables hold `ON DELETE NO ACTION` FKs), so org creation moved into a new atomic `provision_organization()` RPC — org + dispositions + founder attach in one transaction, rolling back the queued Twilio provisioning too. Also fixed: admin gates failing *open* on NULL org (`IF NOT (…)` → `IS NOT TRUE`), a rollback block that would have failed on a signature mismatch, Team Leaders silently losing invitations access, an account-existence oracle, and `invite-user` accepting role strings that would produce permanently unredeemable invitations.

**Files (11, PR #340).** **New:** `supabase/migrations/20260731180000_p0_email_release_blockers.sql`, `supabase/tests/p0_profile_authorization.sql`, `supabase/functions/_shared/organizationProvisioning.ts`, `src/contexts/__tests__/signupPayload.test.tsx`. **Edited:** `supabase/functions/{create-user,invite-user}/index.ts`, `src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx`, `src/pages/SignupPage.tsx`, `src/pages/__tests__/signupPage.test.tsx`, `AGENT_RULES.md` (invariant #20), `WORK_LOG.md`. **`create-organization` is NOT changed by this PR** — deferred. `implementation_plan.md` is not part of PR #340.

**Verification.** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean · `npx vitest run` **532/532** (51 files; 526 baseline + 6 new) · `deno check` clean on `create-user` and `_shared/organizationProvisioning` · `git diff --check` clean. **Known pre-existing failure:** `deno check supabase/functions/invite-user/index.ts` reports `TS2304: Cannot find name 'logoUrl'` — reproduced identically on untouched `origin/main` (this is the live scope bug PR #338 fixes); this branch's diff to that file is +19 lines of role validation only. **Advisors (baseline, pre-migration)** independently corroborate both targets: `rls_policy_always_true` on `public.profiles.profiles_insert` and on `public.invitations.invitations_update_status`; performance advisor also shows the `TO PUBLIC` policies applying to **anon**. Both should disappear post-apply.

**The adversarial SQL matrix has NOT yet been permanently applied or executed against production.** It is committed for review and will be run as a single rolled-back validation transaction immediately before the migration is applied. Not claimed as passing.

**Deferred with a tracked follow-up:** [issue #339](https://github.com/cgarness/agentflow-life-insure/issues/339) — the over-broad `profiles_select_org` read. Verified non-bypass before deferring: anon reads nothing (`get_user_org_id()` is NULL for anon, empirically confirmed) and `profiles` holds no credential column. Also noted, not fixed: the Super Admin Provisioning Wizard's direct browser `organizations` INSERT is **already broken today** (no INSERT policy exists on that table) — pre-existing, needs its own decision.

**Migrations applied: none. Edge deployments: none. Auth/SMTP/secret changes: none. Production data: untouched. Nothing pushed or merged.**
2026-07-30 | [CODE COMPLETE — local branch `claude/system-email-unification`, NOT pushed, NOT merged, NOT deployed; migration NOT applied; no Auth/dashboard change; no test emails sent] SECURITY + DESIGN — System email audit, repair & unification onto one shared renderer

**What & why.** Chris asked for an audit and unification of every AgentFlow-owned transactional email. The live audit (all 7 email Edge Functions fetched via `get_edge_function` and byte-diffed against repo, plus read-only DB/trigger/cron/RLS introspection) found the system in worse shape than the brief assumed: **two emails never delivered at all**, **two endpoints were open internet relays**, and initial vs resent invitations used different functions, different templates (dark glass vs light), and different subjects. This branch fixes all of it behind one shared renderer. **Nothing has been deployed or applied — code only.**

**Audit findings (all verified against live prod, not inferred).**
- **Agency Group invites never delivered.** `invite-to-agency-group` v20 declares `const logoUrl` inside the request handler but references it from module-level `buildEmailHtml()` → `ReferenceError` on *every* send, swallowed by the surrounding try/catch. Invites were recorded with `email_sent:false`; no invitee ever received mail. Repo was byte-identical to live, so the bug was live, not just local.
- **Welcome emails never delivered.** Live `current_setting('app.settings.supabase_url')` and `…service_role_key` both returned **NULL**, so `handle_new_user_welcome_email` hit its guard and `RAISE WARNING`ed on every signup. (Same NULL GUC also breaks cron jobs 1–2 — logged as a separate ops item, deliberately not touched here.)
- **Open relays.** `send-invite-email` and `send-welcome-email` ran `verify_jwt=false` with **zero in-code auth** and CORS `*`; `send-invite-email` accepted an arbitrary recipient, an arbitrary CTA URL, and unescaped HTML fields — anyone on the internet could send `team@fflagent.com`-branded mail.
- **Live/repo drift.** Live `invite-user` still carried the obsolete Lovable fallback `https://preview--life-agent-hub.lovable.app` and a text logo; the **repo** copy had the image logo *plus the same fatal logoUrl scope bug* — deploying repo would have silently killed all invite email. `send-email-previews` repo copy was two revisions stale (live v21 was edited directly in prod on 2026-06-01, never committed). `create-user`, `send-invite-email`, `send-welcome-email`, `invite-to-agency-group`, `workflow-executor` were byte-identical to live.
- No WORK_LOG conflict: the newest prior email decision (2026-06-01 light-mode redesign) is exactly what this continues; it had explicitly skipped `invite-user` and `invite-to-agency-group`.

**Shared renderer (new).** `supabase/functions/_shared/systemEmail.ts` — design tokens, `renderSystemEmail()` → `{html, text}`, `escapeHtml()` (incl. `'`), `sanitizeHeaderText()` (strips CR/LF + control chars from subjects/preheaders), `assertHttpsUrl()` (https-only link guard), `resolveSiteUrl()`/`resolveLogoUrl()`, `SYSTEM_EMAIL_FROM`. Shell is **table-based with inline CSS**, light `#F1F5F9`/560px white card/4px `#2563EB` accent, image logo, hidden preheader, plain-text alternative, **dynamic year**, visible fallback-link box, `@media` mobile padding. `_shared/systemEmailTemplates.ts` holds the four templates; `_shared/systemEmailAuth.ts` holds the in-code caller auth (`authenticateRequest`, `isOrgAdmin`, `canManageOrganization`, `isSuperAdmin`).

**Per-email changes.**
- **`create-user`** — confirmation email via `renderConfirmationEmail`; local `escapeHtml`/`buildConfirmEmailHtml` deleted. Signup flow, invite acceptance, `generateLink`, best-effort semantics, and 200-status response shapes preserved byte-for-byte.
- **`invite-user`** — dark glass template and the scope-bugged `logoUrl` deleted; now renders `renderTeamInvitationEmail` with the caller's org name (best-effort `.maybeSingle()` lookup). Profiles lookup `.single()`→`.maybeSingle()`; raw DB error no longer returned to the client. Auth gate, org-scoped insert, `{invitation_id, token, email_sent}` contract (Copy Link consumes `token`) preserved.
- **`send-invite-email`** — rewritten from open relay to authenticated resend: `POST {invitation_id}` only. JWT + Admin gate, invitation loaded by id, **cross-org callers get the same 404 as a missing row** (no existence disclosure), non-Pending → 409, recipient/name/role/token read **only** from the invitations row, and it renders through the **same** `renderTeamInvitationEmail` as the initial send.
- **`send-welcome-email`** — rewritten as **Option B** JWT self-service: valid user JWT required, **recipient is always the authenticated user's own email** (request body ignored entirely), confirmed email required, and idempotency via an **atomic claim** on `profiles.welcome_email_sent_at` (`.is(null)` + `.select()` — concurrent losers get `already_sent`). Send failure best-effort releases the claim so the user can retry. Stray dark `confirmation_template.txt` deleted.
- **`invite-to-agency-group`** — fatal logoUrl crash fixed by construction; org/group names now escaped in **body and subject**; dead `organization_name` body field dropped. Auth, master-org scoping, duplicate-membership checks, and `email_sent` semantics untouched.

- **`workflow-executor` — UNTOUCHED** (`git diff` empty, verified). Agency-authored workflow email stays unwrapped and tenant-scoped, per product intent. Gmail contact email untouched.

**Frontend.** `sendInviteEmail(invitationId)` replaces the old `{email, firstName, role, inviteURL}` payload (no more `window.location.origin` CTA construction); dead `resendInvite` deleted; `createInvitation` now returns `{id, token}`. `PendingInvitesTable` resends by id; `SuperAdminDashboard` keeps the invitation row on email failure and toasts accurately instead of pushing the wizard into duplicate creation; `InviteUserModal` honors `email_sent` instead of always claiming "email sent". New `useWelcomeEmailTrigger` hook (mounted in `AppLayout`) fires the one-time welcome post-confirmation, guarded by `sessionStorage` and fully silent.

Service-role key is never stored in a Postgres setting.

Rendered all four templates to HTML and inspected them in a real browser at 1280 desktop and 375 mobile: light card, image logo loading from `https://www.fflagent.com/agentflow-logo-full.png` (**confirms the canonical fallback domain actually serves the asset**), badge/heading/CTA/fallback box/footer with live year, welcome feature rows using numbered markers instead of emoji, correct mobile padding with no horizontal overflow. **Injection proof:** rendering with `O'Brien & Sons <script>alert(1)</script>` in first name, role, and org shows the payload as inert visible text, apostrophe intact, and the browser console recorded **zero** entries — nothing executed.

**Adversarial review pass (3 independent lenses: security / correctness-regression / frontend) — 9 real defects found in the first implementation and FIXED before handoff.**
1. **CRITICAL — mass welcome-email send to the entire existing user base.** The migration added `welcome_email_sent_at` with no backfill, so every existing profile read as "not yet welcomed" and would have been mailed on next app load. **Fixed:** the migration now backfills `welcome_email_sent_at = now()` for all existing rows in the same transaction, and the deploy runbook adds a hard gate — `SELECT count(*) FROM profiles WHERE welcome_email_sent_at IS NULL` must return **0** before the frontend ships.
2. **HIGH — welcome claim never released on a thrown exception.** Only the returned-`{error}` branch reset the claim; a transport throw or a render throw left the row stamped, permanently blocking that user's welcome email with no recovery path. **Fixed:** render + send are wrapped so *any* failure mode releases the claim.
3. **HIGH — welcome trigger unreachable for its own audience.** Freshly-confirmed signups are redirected to `/onboarding`, which renders outside `AppLayout`, so a user who never finished the wizard would never receive a welcome email. **Fixed:** the hook is now mounted in `OnboardingShell` as well.
4. **MEDIUM — `email_sent: true` could be a lie.** Resend reports API-level failures via a returned `{ error }` rather than throwing, and `invite-user` / `create-user` / `invite-to-agency-group` discarded it — so the new "email failed" UI branch would never fire. **Fixed:** all three inspect the return value.
5. **MEDIUM — three broken links in the welcome email.** `/support`, `/privacy`, `/terms` are not routes (verified against `App.tsx`); every new user would have hit NotFound. **Fixed:** footer links removed, with a test asserting they stay out until the routes exist.
6. **MEDIUM — SuperAdmin failure toast pointed at an unreachable screen.** Pending Invites is scoped to the viewer's own org and can never show a newly-provisioned agency's invitation. **Fixed:** accurate copy.
7. **LOW — plain-text injection.** The `text/plain` part interpolated names/org raw, so a caller-supplied newline could forge extra lines of "AgentFlow" copy inside a DKIM-signed message. **Fixed centrally** in `renderSystemEmail` (heading + every body line sanitized), with a regression test across all four templates.
8. **LOW — `invite-to-agency-group` leaked raw Postgres error text** to the browser while `invite-user` had been hardened. **Fixed:** generic messages, detail logged server-side.
9. **LOW — server error messages lost in the resend UI.** supabase-js turns any non-2xx into `FunctionsHttpError`, so "Invitation is no longer pending" surfaced as "non-2xx status code". **Fixed:** the function's message is parsed out of the error context.
Also corrected by the review: the deploy order now applies the migration **first** (the function selects a column that must exist), and `deno.lock` was reverted (its churn was Deno-installer and unrelated workspace-package noise).

**Verified-correct by the review (no change needed):** `workflow-executor` completely untouched; Gmail contact path untouched; `create-user` / `invite-user` / `invite-to-agency-group` auth gates, insert field sets, and duplicate-membership checks byte-identical to HEAD; the logoUrl crash genuinely fixed in both functions; the welcome idempotency claim is correctly atomic under READ COMMITTED; the migration is idempotent and nothing else references the dropped trigger/function; `getBearerToken` rejects every whitespace-only/malformed header; no path reaches a Resend send without the in-code gate; no caller-supplied value can influence the recipient in any hardened function.

**Open security finding — NOT fixed here (needs its own approval).** The new in-code gates read `profiles.role` / `profiles.is_super_admin`, and RLS policy **`profiles_update_own` is `UPDATE USING (id = auth.uid())` with NO `WITH CHECK`** — verified live. Any authenticated user can therefore write **any column on their own profile row**, including `role`, `is_super_admin`, and `welcome_email_sent_at`. That makes self-promotion to Admin/super-admin possible today (this predates and is independent of this change — `invite-user` and `invite-to-agency-group` already trusted the same columns), and it also means the welcome email's one-time guard is user-resettable. This belongs with the excluded `create-user` privilege-escalation and invitation-RLS items in a dedicated security plan.

**Migrations: none applied. Edge deployments: none. Supabase Auth/dashboard/SMTP changes: none. Secret/env changes: none. Production test emails: none. Nothing pushed or merged.**

**Deliberately excluded (each needs its own security/ops plan + approval, per Chris 2026-07-30).** `create-user` privilege escalation (anonymous caller can still self-assign `role`/`organization_id` — **the most serious open finding**), the `invitations_update_status` RLS policy (any authenticated user can UPDATE any invitation row where the result is `status='accepted'`), `workflow-executor` cross-tenant `message_templates` lookup, retirement of the dead-but-deployed `accept-invite` function, and the NULL-GUC cron repairs (jobs 1–2).

**Blockers / next steps.** Awaiting Chris's explicit approval for each production action, in this order: (1) apply the welcome migration, (2) deploy the 6 Edge Functions **with `get_edge_function` re-fetched immediately before each deploy** (invariant #4) and the frontend merged in lockstep with `send-invite-email` (contract change), (3) approved preview sends to `cgarness.ffl@gmail.com` for the Gmail/Apple Mail/Outlook-web/Outlook-desktop/mobile matrix, (4) the Auth-template dashboard paste + SMTP inspection. Two facts only Chris can confirm: the `PUBLIC_SITE_URL` Edge secret value (unreadable via MCP) and that `fflagent.com` is the verified Resend sending domain.

- **Fixed after the copy change:** Chris's longer rail copy wraps to two lines at the `lg` boundary, which pushed **134px** of overflow at 1024×700 (a gap the original 1440/1280-only sweep missed — the login column itself stayed fully visible; only the decorative panel spilled). - **Behavior:** empty submit → inline errors + `aria-invalid="true"` + `aria-describedby` wired, `login` never called; **invalid credentials → real Supabase "Invalid login credentials"** rendered in the `role="alert"` region, no navigation; loading state sampled mid-flight = disabled + spinner + "Signing in…", then re-enabled (no duplicate submission); password toggle flips `type` and `aria-pressed`/`aria-label`; forgot-password → "Reset Password" page and signup → `/signup` both navigate.

- **Reduced motion — proven, not assumed:** enumerated the generated CSS; **all** motion carriers (`animate-in`, `fade-in`, `slide-in-from-bottom-2`, `duration-500`, `hover:-translate-y-px`) sit inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. With the cyan bloom removed in the final flat-navy pass, the runtime audit finds exactly **1** active animation: the one-shot entrance. **Nothing loops anywhere on the page**, and nothing animates behind the form.

**What & why.** Chris's production manual test of Contacts Build 6 surfaced 9 findings. **Fixes.**
- **Fix 1 — default scope = My Contacts (strict).** Root cause: `useContactScope` restored the persisted `user_preferences.settings.contactsScope` verbatim, so a prior Agency selection became the landing scope; and there was no `?scope=` parsing. New pure `resolveInitialScope`/`isContactScope` helpers; pref-load no longer applies the stored scope as landing (always "mine" unless a valid + permitted `?scope=` overrides, honored once after `ready`). `Contacts.tsx` parses `searchParams.get("scope")` and passes it to the hook; scope is never written back to the URL on selection.
- **Fix 2 — no flash of My Contacts before Agency Contacts.** Root cause: `setLoading(true)` ran inside the fetch effect (after paint), so one frame painted new scope + stale rows + `loading=false`. Added a render-time `loadedScopeRef`/`scopeStale` gate (the scope the displayed rows were loaded for, stamped in `fetchData`'s `finally`); the spinner shows and the Leads/Clients/Recruits views are withheld while a scope switch is in flight. `silent` refetches don't trip it (same scope).
- **Fix 3 — inline status convert guard (table).** The Leads inline status `<select>` now opens `ConvertLeadModal` (via existing `setConvertLead`) when the chosen stage maps to a `convert_to_client` pipeline stage (`convertStageNames` memo from already-loaded `leadStages`), instead of persisting. `<select value={l.status}>` stays bound so Cancel snaps back — no orphaned status write before conversion (mirrors Dialer invariant #11).
- **Fix 4 — Kanban convert guard.** dnd-kit drag already worked; added `convertToClient` to `KanbanColumnModel` + a pure `resolveDragOutcome` (none/status/convert). `ContactKanbanBoard` routes a convert-stage drop to a new `onConvertRequest` prop (Leads board → `setConvertLead`); boards without it (Recruits) fall back to a plain status move. `ConvertLeadModal.onSuccess` now also `fetchKanban({silent:true})`. No optimistic move → cancel leaves the card; no flash/duplicate.

2026-06-19 | [HOTFIX — shipped to prod] Contacts Build 2 — production TDZ crash on /contacts

**Incident.** Right after the Build 2 deploy, `/contacts` (prod, `www.fflagent.com`) crashed with a full-page Application Error: `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'Si' before initialization`. Caught by the app ErrorBoundary; page unusable.

**Root cause.** A **temporal dead zone** in `src/pages/Contacts.tsx`: `fetchData` (a `useCallback` at ~line 332) listed `sortCol`/`sortDir` in its **dependency array** (~line 521), but the per-tab sort state (`sortByTab` → `activeSort` → `sortCol`/`sortDir`) was declared **later** (~line 641). A deps array is evaluated **eagerly during render**, so it accessed `sortCol` before its `const` initialized. Dev/ESM tolerated the source order; **Rollup's production bundling exposed the TDZ**. `tsc`, the unit suite, and `madge --circular` all passed — none execute the rendered component. Binding identified by mapping the minified `Si` via a local sourcemapped prod build → `const sortCol = activeSort.col`.

**Fix.** Moved the `sortByTab` / `activeSort` / `sortCol` / `sortDir` declarations **above** `fetchData` (into the filter-state block). One file changed: `src/pages/Contacts.tsx` (declaration relocation only — no logic change).

**Regression guard.** New `src/lib/__tests__/contactsRender.test.tsx` — SSR `renderToString(<Contacts/>)` executes the component body (incl. the deps array) with mocked contexts/hooks/supabase + stubbed child components; fails on any "before initialization" error. This catches the class of bug `tsc`/unit/madge missed.

**Ship.** Commit `2ab8894` → PR [#315](https://github.com/cgarness/agentflow-life-insure/pull/315) → merged to `main` (`95de2e9`). Vercel prod build (project `agentflow-life-insure`) passed. **Prod deploy `dpl_EZuxE6UwZUrSCpZ5mXRwXDnu2EVN` → READY**; production alias + `www.fflagent.com` now serve the fixed bundle (`index-B62hB6fx.js`, ≠ the broken `index-BSOMJt01.js`; the doc-only deploy had an identical broken JS hash, so the new hash proves the fix is live). No DB/RLS/Edge/Twilio/schema change — frontend only.

**Verification.** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean · `npx vitest run` **253/253** (+1 render guard) · targeted ESLint 0 errors · `git diff --check` clean. Unrelated working-tree files left untouched.

**Follow-up / lesson.** tsc does not flag a `const` referenced in a `useCallback`/`useMemo` dependency array before its declaration; the production bundler turns it into a hard crash. The new SSR render smoke test is the guard. (Build 3 could extend render smoke coverage to other heavy pages.)

2026-06-17 | [SORTING CORRECTION — migration PENDING APPLY] Contacts Build 2 — Client/Recruit Assigned-Agent sort moved to RPC (LEFT JOIN; unassigned kept)

**Pre-apply fix (Chris) — verification blocker on Client/Recruit "Assigned Agent" sort.** The prior pass sorted clients/recruits by agent via PostgREST `.order(col, { referencedTable })`. Per PostgREST, ordering a *referenced* table only reorders the **parent** rows when embedded with **`!inner`** — and `!inner` would **exclude unassigned** clients/recruits, which must remain visible in Agency Contacts. So that approach was unreliable (either didn't sort parents, or dropped unassigned). **Replaced with server-side RPCs.**

**Fix.** Six new SECURITY INVOKER functions in the same migration (mirroring leads): `_contacts_filtered_clients`/`_contacts_filtered_recruits` (the canonical filtered+ordered `(id, ord)` set), `search_contacts_clients`/`search_contacts_recruits` (page jsonb rows + exact total), `contacts_client_ids_matching`/`contacts_recruit_ids_matching` (`(id, ord)` for select-all). Each uses a SQL **LEFT JOIN public.profiles** → `agent_sort` (displayed agent name; **unassigned/missing profile → NULL → NULLS LAST**, both directions). Allowlisted **static CASE** sort (no dynamic SQL): clients = name(case-insensitive last,first)/phone/email/state/policy_type/carrier/issue_date(text→chrono)/premium+face_amount(**numeric**)/assigned_agent/created_at; recruits = name/phone/email/state/status/assigned_agent/created_at. `created_at DESC, id DESC` default + deterministic id tie-break. **No `!inner`; no PostgREST referenced-table ordering remains anywhere.** RLS + org scope preserved (INVOKER). Ordinary own-column sorts also run server-side via the same RPC (before LIMIT/OFFSET).

**Frontend.** `clientsSupabaseApi`/`recruitsSupabaseApi` `getAll` → `search_contacts_*` RPC (rows + total); `getAllIdsMatching` → `contacts_*_ids_matching` with `.order("ord").range()` chunked loop (uncapped, gap/dupe-free, same order as visible rows). Removed the broken embed/`referencedTable` order code + the now-unused `CLIENT/RECRUIT_SORT_DB_COLUMNS`. `bulkAssign`/`deleteAllMatching`/`getById`/CRUD unchanged (base tables). Page wiring unchanged (still passes canonical `sortColumn`/`sortDirection`).

**Tests (`contactsSort.test.ts` rewritten).** Added an **Assigned-Agent ordering spec** over an A/B/**unassigned** fixture proving: ascending (by agent, unassigned LAST), descending (unassigned still LAST), **unassigned preserved both directions**, NULLS-LAST placement, **>1 page** consistency (full-dataset order then slice), and created_at→id tie-break. Plus RPC-path tests: clients/recruits `getAll` call `search_contacts_*` with the sort in `p_filters`; `getAllIdsMatching` call `contacts_*_ids_matching` ordered by `ord` (parity), >1000 ids dupe-free across ranges. `contactsBulkSafety` clients/recruits ids tests updated to the RPC path.

**Confirmed:** the query does **NOT** use `!inner`; it uses a SQL LEFT JOIN — unassigned rows are kept. Ordinary Client/Recruit own-column sorting remains server-side before pagination (same RPC).

Last Disposition uses the **same** linked set so display (now from RPC scalars) and filter agree. TS reference spec `callBelongsToLead`/`countLeadCallAttempts`/`matchesAttemptBucket` added to `contactsFilters.ts` and tested (legacy contact_id counts; future lead_id counts; both→once; non-lead excluded; foreign lead_id excluded; **exactly 4 → 4+**).
2. **Duplicate index removed.** Prod already has `idx_calls_lead_id` AND `idx_calls_contact_id` (both linkage branches covered) + the `idx_leads_*` set. The proposed `CREATE INDEX idx_calls_lead_id` was a duplicate and is **removed**; **no index added.** Any need is gated on a checkpoint-2 `EXPLAIN` (before/after plans shown first).
3. **Downline helper → SECURITY INVOKER.** `get_contact_scope_agents` changed from DEFINER to **SECURITY INVOKER**. The `WHERE (id = auth.uid() OR is_ancestor_of(auth.uid(), id)) AND organization_id = get_org_id()` does the hierarchy + org scoping; existing profiles RLS supplies per-role visibility (Agent→self, TL→self+descendants, Admin→org, Super Admin→home org), and `is_ancestor_of` (itself DEFINER) yields the Admin downline subset — so INVOKER returns exactly self+downline with no widening, no caller-supplied org, names/ids only, REVOKE PUBLIC + authenticated-only. **All four functions are now SECURITY INVOKER.** (The DEFINER justification in the entry below is withdrawn.)

**Revised migration `20260617180000_contacts_scope_search_rpcs.sql` — function inventory (all `public`, `LANGUAGE sql`, `STABLE`, `SECURITY INVOKER`, `SET search_path = public, pg_temp`, `REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC` + `GRANT EXECUTE TO authenticated`):** `_contacts_filtered_leads(jsonb)` (the one shared WHERE; RLS-narrowed scope; compatibility attempt/disposition linkage), `search_contacts_leads(jsonb)→jsonb` (page rows + exact `total_count`), `contacts_lead_ids_matching(jsonb)→SETOF uuid`, `get_contact_scope_agents()→TABLE(id,first_name,last_name)`.
